ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-18): "nsvpx" has NO entry in this table (nor in taxonomy.py's
detector aliases beyond the vendor mapping), so get_profile("nsvpx-12.0.53.13")
matched nothing and fell through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (512MB RAM / 1 vCPU).
Live-reproduced booting the real local image (nsvpx-12.0.53.13/virtioa.qcow2) at
that 512MB fallback: the FreeBSD-based loader gets all the way into the NetScaler
kernel (ns_physmem_init reserves only ~38MB for NetScaler use out of the 512MB
total) and then the kernel OOM-kills its own boot processes outright -
"pid 22 (pitboss), uid 0, was killed: out of swap space" / same for pid 23 (sh) -
both within ~40s of power-on, confirmed via the real QEMU serial console, not a
mock. docs/platform/node-emulation.md already documents Citrix's real minimum
(2048MB RAM, 4 vCPU) from the vendor datasheet - it was simply never wired into
this table (DoD step 5, rule #14, was skipped for this device). RAM/CPU bumped to
match; disk_bus kept at "virtio" (NOT the "ide" the doc footnote mentions for a
freshly-converted raw vendor image) because the actual locally-imported artifact
is already named virtioa.qcow2 and the live boot confirms the virtio disk reads
fine (loader loads the kernel/modules, kernel probes ATA/USB, gets to
"Trying to mount root from ufs:/dev/md0c" - the failure is purely OOM, never a
disk/bus mismatch) - flipping the bus to ide would break a currently-working disk
path to chase a doc footnote that predates this locally-converted image.

reasons.emulator:
cpu_model "qemu64", not "host" (2026-09-12, Wave 21 close, netplex rule #43 - EVE-NG
first, never guess): EVE-NG's own nsvpx.yml qemu_options has NO `-cpu` flag at all
(`-machine type=pc,accel=kvm ... -rtc base=utc`) - it runs this OS on QEMU's plain
default CPU model, not host-passthrough. `cpu_model_for()`'s own docstring already
documents this exact failure class for another old-kernel appliance (AireOS/vWLC's
3.10 kernel: "can kernel-panic on host-passthrough's exposed feature/clock set;
pinning a conservative model avoids that"). NetScaler's kernel here is an equally
old FreeBSD derivative. Two things were tried and live-reproduced this session,
in order, being honest about what did and didn't work (rule #22): (1) cpu 4->2
(matching EVE-NG's vCPU count) did NOT change the symptom - reproduced identically
with cpu=2: SMP brings up fine ("SMP: AP CPU #1 Launched!"), reaches "Trying to
mount root from ufs:/dev/md0c" / "NS-KERN /dev/md0 for compatibilty", then total
serial silence for the rest of the 600s budget, byte-identical to the cpu=4 case.
So vCPU count is NOT the cause - ruled out with evidence, not assumed. (2) Not yet
live-verified this session: switching cpu_model to "qemu64" (matching EVE-NG's
real no-passthrough config) - the next thing to try before guessing further, since
the vCPU-count hypothesis is now ruled out and machine/cpu-model divergence is the
next real difference from EVE-NG's own working template.
